100% agree!
I would talk to the Nephrologist.
There are so many different situations.
Some have more problems with protein in the urine, others with blood.
The egfr without other variables is not very meaningful.
What’s the creatinine levels, is there acidosis… And so many more.
So: thinking about medication without a WIDE back knowledge isn’t helpful at all.
If in doubt get a second or third opinion (I did that and with my 2nd nephrologist I have a lottery win!
He knows all new studies and makes informed decisions with my consent and if in doubt talks to other nephrologists!)
IGAN is not automatically a death sentence.
Nor is every case fast progressing.
Take a deep breath and don’t try things just because it seems to be the wonder drug.
I wish both of you the best!
And I totally get that you are worried.

Meds are of a for life thing.
As others had mentioned since there is no cure the drugs are there to try to suppress the damage this disease can do to the body .
IgAN is a disease that can lead to end stage renal failure .
Starting medication when the damage is presenting itself is to delay that as much as possible .
I have always been hesitant about the utilization of steroids like prednisone as for me the benefit hasn’t outweighed the risk for this disease .
The benefits are temporary and the risks are things you have to deal with long term .
My best friend has had amazing results with Filspari , his blood work and quality of life did a full 180 and he started the drug when he was already at end stage .
About 2 -3 months after the drug is started is when you see the most substantial jump in your bloodwork balancing itself off .

We were planning for dialysis at that time actually and his MD said he wanted us to always be prepared for the potential of it being necessary but it wasn’t something we had to start with how big of a change he saw .
That was about a year and a half ago , he never needed dialysis and is getting a transplant in 2 months.
It’s always good to be on top of alternative or additional therapies out there as everything made for this disease is so new and your MD might not have it on their radar just yet .

Silbeprenlimab hasn’t been approved by EMA or MHRA yet.
Budesonide is available in UK and EU.

It is a relatively new medication which is a corticosteroid that is designed in IgA medication to only target the part of your bowels that produce a lot of the IgA proteins that our bodies cannot remove.
If you can tolerate it is quite an exciting drug therapy as it directly targets the disease.
It is not a cure but the studies have shown positive results in both slowing down damage to the kidneys and reducing proteinuria significantly.
Another one that is approved in UK and EU is Sparsentan with the brand name Filspari.
That is also specifically approved for IgA management.
It helps with a lot of the downstream effects of IgAN.
Including the proteinuria and high blood pressure if you have it.
At the moment they are generally being recommended for use in patients with high risk of rapid disease progression.
So if your Renal Doctor suggests using it then it is sensible to take them.
The doc hasn’t prescribed or suggested budesonide yet, only lisinopril, simvastatin and forxiga for now. I suppose they will review in 3 months when I have my next tests.
That is all fairly standard first line treatment and lines up to what I was prescribed when diagnosed.
Lisinopril is a type of drug called an ACE Inhibitor which is primarily for treating high blood pressure, which is common in IgAN patients.
This helps protect your kidneys and overall health.
The clinical evidence also shows these drugs also protect your kidneys for longer.
Simvastatin helps reduce cholesterol levels in your blood, which helps protect our kidneys.
And statins have further benefits to helping protect your kidney health.
Forxiga is a SGLT2 inhibitor which helps with reducing the pressure on your kidneys leading to help protect them, which also should reduce the amount of proteinuria you have.
All three are super important first line medications to help keep you healthy for longer.
It is important to take them everyday consistently.
